title: The road to Brahman
hookLine: Krishna draws the whole road to Brahman, and finds love at the top

cards: Picture the scene the blind king is hearing about. Two armies have stood on the field at Kurukshetra this whole time, conches blown, bows raised, waiting, while a charioteer and a prince talk between the lines.
Seventeen chapters of questions. Now Krishna does what a guide does near the end of a long climb: he stops and draws the whole road at once.
In about ten verses it runs from ordinary work, done without clinging, all the way to Brahman, the ultimate reality. And at the top, there's a surprise.

teach.b: Verse forty-nine: with understanding unattached everywhere, self mastered, desire gone, a person reaches through relinquishment the highest perfection, freedom from the bind of action.
Verse fifty: now hear, briefly, how the one who's reached that perfection reaches Brahman. Then the road, verses fifty-one to fifty-three. A clear understanding.

Holding yourself steady with resolve. Setting aside sound and the other sense objects, putting down liking and disliking. Seeking quiet, solitary places, eating lightly, speech, body and mind held in check.
Always turning to meditation, resting in dispassion. Letting go of ego, force, pride, desire, anger, and the need to own things.

teach.h: STEADY: SIMPLE, QUIET, FREE OF MINE.
teach.b: Free of mine, at peace. That one, Krishna says, is fit to become Brahman. The word that holds it together is dhriti, steadiness, resolve.
Not a burst of effort. A steady hand. Then verse fifty-four, the summit, and a surprise.

Having become Brahman, serene, that person neither grieves nor craves. The same toward all beings, they reach the highest love for me. One might expect the road to end in a merging where love disappears.
Here, on becoming Brahman, love begins. Verse fifty-five: by love they know me as I truly am, and knowing me, they enter me.

Advaita teachers read this as knowledge completing itself; Vaishnava teachers read it as devotion as the goal. Both keep the verse, and in its own words the summit isn't a blank: it's love. Then Krishna turns to Arjuna.
Verse fifty-seven: give all your actions to me in your mind.
Verse fifty-eight: with your mind on me, by my grace you'll cross every obstacle.
But if, out of ego, you won't listen, you'll be lost.

how: Some Hindu teachers read Gita 18.49–18.58 as a summary of the whole spiritual path, from unattached work and disciplined living to realizing Brahman and supreme devotion (para bhakti).

o: born into a family of Brahmin priests
having become Brahman, serene and steady
a spirit that lingers on after death

games.q: the road, verse by verse — tap the pairs.
p: by my grace you'll cross every obstacle

s: in Gita 18.54, love disappears once a person becomes Brahman
the verse says that having become Brahman, they reach the highest love.
the road includes eating lightly and seeking solitude
verses 51–53: a quiet, solitary life, free of mine.
verse 58 warns that ego that won't listen leads to being lost
by grace you cross; out of ego, you're lost.

games.q: you've become Brahman, serene, the same toward all beings. what does verse 54 say comes next?
o: the highest love for the divine.
games.why: the highest love. and verse 55: by love they know him as he is, and enter him.

practice: Try one piece of the road, steadiness: spine upright, breath even. When a sound comes, let it pass without liking or disliking it; when a thought of mine comes, my plans, my things, let it pass too.
Don't force anything; just hold steady, like a hand around a cup of water, firm but not tight.

wordCard.voice: Brahmabhuta, having become Brahman. Gita eighteen, forty-nine to fifty-eight: relinquishment, steadiness, a quiet, solitary life free of mine, becoming Brahman, and then the highest love.

orig.note: Sanskrit: brahmabhuta, having become Brahman; the summit of the road in Gita 18.54.

carryVoice: Your line: becoming Brahman, love begins. Steady on the road, and love at the summit. See you tomorrow.

sources.ref: Bhagavad Gita 18.49–18.53 (the road: perfection, steadiness, a simple life)
Bhagavad Gita 18.54–18.56 (becoming Brahman; the highest devotion)
Bhagavad Gita 18.57–18.58 (give all actions to me; by my grace)
